facts.condition: For the canonical channel, any finite-auxiliary construction whose two-use Marton functional exceeds two copies of the optimal single-use randomized time-sharing benchmark must place nonzero input-law mass on each paired state 00, 01, 10, and 11.
Under that same strict-improvement premise, the masses on 00 and 11 each exceed 1/180, while those on 01 and 10 each exceed 1/325.

assumptions: The paired-state labels refer to the four super-inputs formed from two uses of the canonical half-skew BSSC.
The comparison concerns the unnormalized two-use Marton functional and the repeated optimum within the stated single-use randomized time-sharing class.
Only necessity is asserted: these support conditions neither establish that an improving construction exists nor imply an unrestricted block-code converse.
